description: Renaissance art, Greek mythology, opera, astronomy, medicine, deep time, architecture, literature, stamp design and Welsh geography define a run built around highly recognisable subjects that become much less comfortable under exact questioning.

s09e01.description: Donatello brings Renaissance sculpture into the hot seat, with several centuries of artistic reputation compressed into one answer. The episode’s broader trivia makes a familiar name compete against the awkward requirement of knowing exactly why it is familiar.

s09e02.description: Cerberus guards the episode with three heads and excellent branding. Greek mythology provides the standout creature while the wider ladder ranges through science, language and culture, none of which comes with a convenient mythological watchdog.

s09e03.description: ‘Sull’aria’ gives the episode an elegant operatic identity. Classical music enters the ladder through a phrase more likely to be sung than spoken, surrounded by the usual Millionaire mixture of knowledge that refuses to stay in one key.

s09e04.description: ‘The Bringer of Peace’ lends the episode a grand musical and astronomical flavour without needing the planet’s name in the title. The phrase hangs memorably above a ladder that is considerably less peaceful for anyone answering it.

s09e05.description: Digitalis gives botany and medicine a beautifully precise shared word. A plant-derived term becomes the episode’s defining curiosity while the rest of the ladder demonstrates how quickly familiar-looking scientific vocabulary can become hostile.

s09e06.description: The Paleozoic era stretches the episode’s timeline back hundreds of millions of years. Deep time joins contemporary general knowledge on the same ladder, making the difference between ancient geology and yesterday’s trivia feel almost administratively small.

s09e07.description: Bellatrix supplies a name shared by astronomy and modern popular imagination. The episode exploits exactly that sort of layered familiarity, moving through a question set where recognition is abundant but precise context remains stubbornly rationed.

s09e08.description: A gargoyle peers down from the episode’s architectural trivia with the appropriate amount of menace. Buildings, culture and general knowledge mingle on a ladder where decorative stonework is somehow permitted to judge people back.

s09e09.description: Ulysses brings an ancient hero, a literary landmark and a famously overloaded name into the quiz. The episode’s wider questions continue the theme of making apparently familiar references much less comfortable when context suddenly matters.

s09e10.description: The Machin Series turns an everyday piece of British visual design into specialised trivia. It is the sort of object millions have encountered without naming, making it almost perfectly engineered for Millionaire’s particular strain of annoyance.

s09e11.description: Red Wharf Bay gives the episode a striking piece of Welsh geography. A place-name with instant atmosphere anchors a broad ladder, where knowing Britain well still leaves plenty of room for one coastline to become surprisingly consequential.
